title: Indian-Origin Leaders Hold Key Roles as Anthropic Heads for Its IPO
excerpt: From CFO Krishna Rao, who signed the IPO filing, to Bengaluru-born CTO Rahul Patil and Claude Code co-creator Sid Bidasaria, Indian-origin executives sit at the centre of Anthropic's finances, technology and governance as it prepares to list.
body:
• Anthropic unveiled its US IPO filing on October 26, reporting revenue of $16.29 billion for the six months ended June 2026, up from $1.16 billion a year earlier, according to Reuters.
  • CFO Krishna Rao, who joined in 2024 after leading finance at Fanatics Commerce and holding a senior corporate development role at Airbnb, oversees the company's finances into the listing.
  • Bengaluru-born Rahul Patil became chief technology officer in October 2025, succeeding co-founder Sam McCandlish; Sid Bidasaria co-created Claude Code, a key revenue driver.
  • Indian-American Neil 'Buddy' Shah chairs Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust, the body that can select and remove most board members.

As Anthropic prepares for one of the largest technology listings on record, several of the people running its finances, infrastructure and governance are of Indian origin — a fact the company's IPO filing has now put in plain view.

Anthropic unveiled its filing for a US initial public offering on Monday, according to Reuters, setting up a market debut that will test investor willingness to fund the AI company's spending. The Claude maker had submitted a confidential filing in June and is targeting a mid-November listing, Reuters reported in its factbox on the filing.

The Indian-origin leadership

Krishna Rao, chief financial officer. Rao joined Anthropic in 2024 as CFO, arriving from Fanatics Commerce, where he held the same role, and earlier spent years at Airbnb as global head of corporate and business development, according to the Reuters factbox. As CFO he is the executive steering the company's finances through the offering.

Rahul Patil, chief technology officer. Bengaluru-born Patil became CTO in October 2025, succeeding co-founder Sam McCandlish, who moved to a chief architect role. Patil was previously CTO of Stripe and, before that, senior vice president of cloud infrastructure at Oracle — experience running large-scale, reliability-critical systems that maps directly onto Anthropic's compute-heavy business.

Sid Bidasaria co-created Claude Code, the coding product that has become a key revenue driver for the company, while Neil 'Buddy' Shah, an Indian-American, chairs the Long-Term Benefit Trust — the governance body with authority to select and remove most board members, an unusual structure that gives the trust lasting influence over the listed company.

Growth, costs and the talent warning

The filing shows why the leadership bench matters. Anthropic's revenue grew to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million a year earlier, and reached $16.29 billion in the six months ended June 2026, Reuters reported. A majority of revenue comes from businesses paying per use for its models, alongside paid Pro and Max subscription tiers.

The prospectus also carries a warning with direct diaspora relevance: changes to immigration policies that restrain the flow of professional and technical talent, including US immigration policies, may inhibit the company's ability to recruit and retain highly qualified employees. The AI industry relies heavily on Indian engineers, many working on H-1B visas — a dependence now disclosed, in writing, to public-market investors.

What to watch

Anthropic, founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, is expected to list in mid-November. Pricing will show how public investors value its growth against its costs — and Rao, Patil and their colleagues will be the team answering for both after the debut.
